findings.claim: The new read rule says entries that translate to one id count once 'by the merge rule of item 6', but item 6 is the shared contract's merge rule only if the numbered items match; the SKILL.md step 6 holds the earliest-timestamp rule and the contract item 6 is not visible in this diff. If item 6 is not the merge rule, the cross-reference is dangling. Also on resolve failure the read cannot translate ids, so the read-count rule and the resolve-failure rule (counts unchanged) are unreconciled for a record mixing engram and memorycard ids of the same occurrence.

Step 5 now defers to 'step 6' for the resolve invocation, and the one-call form with `--key <n> [--key <n2> ...]` is shown only there. The removed command in step 5 was the form tested by the contract; the test now only asserts the indirect text, so nothing pins the exact command in step 6, and the new command form is not covered by any requireText.

evidence: Diff reviewed in full: three files, prose contract and its text-pinning tests.
